metadata.title: A Supersonic Plane Never Hears Its Own Boom
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: At the speed of sound, the Doppler formula predicts an infinite pitch. What really happens?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: For a source approaching a listener, the observed frequency is f s times v, over v minus v s. As a plane's speed approaches the speed of sound, that denominator shrinks toward zero, and the predicted frequency grows without bound. What actually happens at the speed of sound, and beyond it?
beats.new_visual_element: A grey jet, side view, flying right, emitting teal circular wavefronts at a fixed interval, each centred where the plane was when it was emitted (bunched ahead). Top: f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s) = f_s/(1 - M) with a live readout of M climbing from 0.5 toward 1 and the matching multiple of f_s growing.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: plane, wavefronts, Doppler formula with live M and f_o readouts

beats.narration_text: At the speed of sound, the plane keeps pace with every wave it emits. Each new wavefront begins exactly where the earlier fronts have just arrived, so in front of the plane they all pile up together. A listener ahead would receive them all at the same instant. That is what the infinite frequency means.
beats.new_visual_element: M reaches 1. All wavefronts touch at the nose; a gold wall perpendicular to the flight path forms there. The f_o readout is replaced by a crimson infinity.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: plane at M = 1, rings stacked at the nose, gold wall, formula showing infinity

beats.narration_text: Faster than sound, the plane outruns its own waves. Every wavefront still spreads as a sphere, but the plane is always ahead of the newest one. The fronts reinforce one another along two straight lines trailing behind the plane, a cone in three dimensions. This is the shock wave, and its half angle obeys sine theta equals v over v s, one over the Mach number.
beats.new_visual_element: M climbs to 1.5. The gold wall folds back into a V-shaped cone whose edges are tangent to every ring. The Doppler formula fades; sin(theta) = v/v_s = 1/M appears with a marked angle theta at the nose (about 42 degrees at M = 1.5).
beats.accumulated_scene_state: plane at M = 1.5, rings inside a gold Mach cone, angle theta marked, sin(theta) = 1/M

beats.narration_text: The cone travels with the plane. Where it meets the ground, it sweeps forward at the plane's speed, and each listener it passes hears one sharp crack, the sonic boom. Every listener hears it after the plane has already passed overhead, and the boom continues for as long as the flight is supersonic, not only at the moment the plane crosses the speed of sound.
beats.new_visual_element: A ground line with listeners carried past beneath the plane. A dashed line marks the point directly below the plane; a crimson burst appears at each listener only when the cone's lower edge reaches them, well behind the plane.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: plane, faint rings, Mach cone, ground with listeners, below-plane marker, crimson boom bursts

beats.narration_text: The infinite frequency was never a real tone. Beyond the speed of sound, the waves no longer arrive one after another. They arrive together, as a single shock front, heard once by each listener as it sweeps past. The plane stays ahead of that front, so its own boom never reaches it.
beats.new_visual_element: Summary at top: a crossed-out crimson infinity beside NOT AN INFINITE PITCH: ONE SHOCK FRONT. Plane, cone, ground and booms continue.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: summary, plane, Mach cone, ground with boom bursts behind the plane
